title: KMS rotation: dual-read decrypt window with bounded fallback + metrics
author: Emily Zhao
release_notes:
- Adds dual-read decrypt behavior during KMS key rotation (new key first, bounded fallback to old key)
- Adds metrics and tracing attributes to quantify fallback and rotation health
- Introduces config flags to safely roll out per-environment/tenant
body:
Context: As part of ENG-4230 we need a low-downtime rotation path for encrypted artifacts without requiring an immediate full re-encryption sweep. During a scheduled or emergency rotation, we will temporarily accept ciphertext that may have been produced with either the newly-selected key version or the previous key version.

This PR implements a "dual-read" window for decrypt operations in the data plane: attempt decrypt using the active (new) key first, then (conditionally) attempt decrypt with the immediately-previous key as a bounded fallback. This is intentionally limited in scope/time to reduce blast radius and avoid masking misconfiguration.

Behavior summary (decrypt path): 1) Determine active encryption key selector from resolved tenant config (key id + pinned version) 2) Attempt decrypt with active selector 3) If decrypt fails with an eligible error class AND dual-read is enabled AND within rotation window, attempt decrypt with previous selector (one additional call max) 4) On success via fallback, emit metrics + trace attributes and include "fallback_used=true" in structured logs (sanitized) 5) On failure, return original error (with a synthesized "rotation_fallback_attempted" detail for debugging).

Boundaries/guards: - Only one fallback attempt (no chains) - Only to the immediately-previous selector (not arbitrary historical versions) - Fallback only when `kms.rotation.dual_read.enabled` is true and `kms.rotation.dual_read.window_seconds > 0` - Fallback is disabled by default and gated behind a runtime-config flag; additionally can be enabled for a small allowlist of tenants in staging/canary - Error filtering: fallback only triggers on error classes consistent with key mismatch / invalid ciphertext (e.g., InvalidCiphertext/BadRequest for provider wrappers). Explicitly does NOT fallback on throttling/timeouts/AccessDenied to avoid doubling load during outages and to keep IAM/policy problems visible.

Metrics/tracing: - `kms_decrypt_total{provider,tenant_tier,result}` (result=success|failure) - `kms_decrypt_fallback_total{provider,reason}` (reason=invalid_ciphertext|unknown) - `kms_decrypt_fallback_latency_ms` histogram - `kms_rotation_dual_read_window_active` gauge (1 when window is active in process config) - Trace attributes: `kms.key_selector.active`, `kms.key_selector.previous` (hashed), `kms.fallback_used`, `kms.provider_error_code`

Notes: - This PR does not change the encrypt path selection rules; it consumes the control-plane-provided resolved config that includes both active and previous selectors (wired in earlier work). - The previous selector is carried only for the duration of the dual-read window and is not persisted into long-lived caches beyond the configured TTL.

Rollout plan: - Stage behind flags in staging, enable for a single canary tenant, verify fallback rates remain <0.5% after the first 24h following rotation, and ensure no p95 decrypt latency regression >5ms when fallback disabled. - Coordinate with SRE (Sean) for alerting thresholds; initial alerts will be on fallback rate spikes and any sustained increase in decrypt errors.

Test plan: - Unit tests for fallback eligibility (error filtering, window boundaries, one-attempt constraint) - Integration test against KMS stub that simulates ciphertext produced by prior key version - Load test verifies no measurable regression when dual-read disabled; verifies bounded overhead when enabled (max +1 KMS call for small % of requests)

Follow-ups: - Wire SRE dashboards/alerts (ENG-4239) to include fallback rates by tenant tier - Document rotation semantics in ADR-0142 and operator runbooks once final thresholds are confirmed
commits: kms: add DualReadDecryptor wrapper with bounded fallback
kms: classify provider error codes for fallback eligibility
config: add kms.rotation.dual_read.* flags + tenant allowlist
metrics: emit fallback counters/histograms + trace attributes
tests: unit + integration coverage for dual-read window
conversation: Marcus Lin (review): Can we confirm we are NOT falling back on AccessDenied / throttling? We can't double KMS calls during an outage and we don't want IAM regressions masked.

Emily Zhao (author): Yep. Fallback eligibility is limited to our InvalidCiphertext-like class (provider-specific mapping). Throttle/timeout/AccessDenied short-circuit and return the original error. Added tests to prevent widening this in the future.
Vikram Singh (review): Please ensure the previous key selector isn't cached longer than the rotation window. If a process never restarts, this could turn into a long-term bypass.

Emily Zhao (author): Good catch. Previous selector is only present in the resolved config and we apply a hard window check on every decrypt attempt. Also bounded the in-memory selector cache TTL to `min(selector_cache_ttl, window_seconds)` when dual-read is on.
Allison Grant (review): Metrics look good. Can we add a label or trace attribute to distinguish 'fallback attempted but failed' vs 'fallback succeeded'? Helps during canaries.
Emily Zhao (author): Added `kms.fallback_attempted` trace attr and a `kms_decrypt_fallback_total{result=success|failure}` split (kept cardinality low; no tenant id).
Sean Gallagher (review): What happens if ciphertext is corrupted and triggers eligible fallback every time? We could add 1 extra KMS call per request permanently for bad payloads.

Emily Zhao (author): True during the dual-read window. Outside the window there's no fallback. Within the window, it's bounded to one extra call; also added a local negative cache for (ciphertext_hash -> non-fallbackable) when we see repeated failures that are clearly not key-mismatch. Kept it conservative and scoped to 60s TTL.
Ethan Park (review): Please add a link in flags.md describing recommended rollout steps + how to scope to canary tenants.
Emily Zhao (author): Added. Also included a note about keeping window small (default 6h recommended) and monitoring fallback rate thresholds.
